⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **170** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b3098661cd3ad78634dd77a31ae68530ab9a3a83` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `aee0ec42e824fc6ce330c5bb16a8ce91956a7a1a` — the merge of head `2efc7b56d9b756146e70ba928f2d3a4b0d8d61c5` into base `b3098661cd3ad78634dd77a31ae68530ab9a3a83`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin aee0ec42e824fc6ce330c5bb16a8ce91956a7a1a && git checkout aee0ec42e824fc6ce330c5bb16a8ce91956a7a1a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b3098661cd3ad78634dd77a31ae68530ab9a3a83 2efc7b56d9b756146e70ba928f2d3a4b0d8d61c5 && git checkout -B drift-repro b3098661cd3ad78634dd77a31ae68530ab9a3a83 && git merge --no-ff 2efc7b56d9b756146e70ba928f2d3a4b0d8d61c5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b3098661cd3ad78634dd77a31ae68530ab9a3a83
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b3098661cd3ad78634dd77a31ae68530ab9a3a83` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2efc7b56d9b756146e70ba928f2d3a4b0d8d61c5`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts + packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts (the disable branch on `main`, read as the door the row names), packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts (the standard catalog and `HttpStatusErrorCodeMap`), packages/spec/src/api/retired-error-codes.ts, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs and AGENTS.md "Add a changeset" (the level rule the changeset is graded by). The rest of the diff (two pin tests, three regenerated reference pages, one changeset) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Inputs read: card #30724 (body; comments 6672694111, 6673430391, 6674977179), the ruling 6670643454 on #30379 and the #30379 body, PR #30775 (body, file list, net diff `origin/main...2efc7b56d9`, 7 files, +59/-3), the check-runs on the head.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set widens by one literal** — `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER['@objectstack/runtime']` gains `PACKAGE_DISABLE_RESTRICTED_BY_VALIDATION_RULE` (`error-code-ledger.zod.ts:515` at the head), so `REGISTERED_ERROR_CODES`, `RegisteredErrorCode`, `ErrorCode`, `ApiErrorSchema.code`, every envelope built on `BaseResponseSchema`, and `FlowInnerRefusal.code` (`automation-api.zod.ts`) accept it. Right: this is exactly what ruling 6670643454 item 3 orders ("`409` with a new error code; the ledger entry is a `domain:spec` card"), and the ledger header (`error-code-ledger.zod.ts:93-103`) names registration a widening of the published face. No existing code moves; the generated pages' `+360 more` → `+361 more` is the same one literal.
- **Scope rule** (`:19-54`): the owner key is `@objectstack/runtime`, a package published from this repo, and it is the package that owns the door (`packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts:1950-1981`). Right. No second door exists: `packages/rest` mounts no `PATCH /packages/:id/disable` (read `rest-server.ts` on `main`), so one row is the whole provenance once the stamp lands.
- **Alphabetical place**: after `PACKAGE_DELETE_PARTIAL` (`:495` on `main`), before `PROJECT_MEMBERSHIP_REQUIRED`. Right. (The runtime block is not sorted end to end — `API_KEY_`/`ANALYTICS_`/`ACTION_` lead it and `MIXED_ARTIFACT_COLLECTION_SHAPE` closes it — and no gate asserts order; `REGISTERED_ERROR_CODES` is a computed sorted union, `error-code-ledger.test.ts:54`.)
- **Standard-synonym detector** (`standardSynonymOf`, `:1923-1936` on `main`): prong 1 — the code is no RFC reason phrase; prong 2 — tokens `PACKAGE`, `DISABLE`, `RESTRICTED`, `BY`, `VALIDATION`, `RULE` are not all carried by any one `StandardErrorCode` member (`PACKAGE` and `DISABLE` appear in none). Verdict `undefined`, so no `STANDARD_SYNONYM_WAIVERS` entry is owed. Right; the pin's control leg `RESTRICTED_DELETE` → `DELETE_RESTRICTED` is a true positive of prong 2, so the `undefined` is a verdict.
- **Provenance** (`check:error-code-provenance`, header `:138-148`): no stamp site exists on `main` (`git grep` of the spelling on `origin/main` is empty), so no `PROVENANCE_WAIVERS` entry and no second owner row is owed. Right. The producerless row is the declared split shape (`ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`, `:362-372`; `FLOW_INPUT_SCHEMA_INVALID`, `:443-451`): a card number behind it (#30379, named in the row), not the "registered but unemittable" retirement class (`:150-180`).
- **Status and guidance tables**: `HttpStatusErrorCodeMap` (`errors.zod.ts:183-197`) is standard-catalog only; the status-conformance gate reconciles ledger codes only once a page publishes a status for them (`check-error-status-conformance.mjs:87-95`: the residual is "a subtraction, not a promise"); `dispatcher-error-vocabulary.ts` carries no `pending-registration` row for the code; `check-error-code-casing.mjs` has no code table. None owes a row today. Right.
- **Retired codes**: `retired-error-codes.ts` retires only `CONCURRENT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`; the spelling collides with nothing retired or live. Right.
- **Name against the ledger's practice** (`:56-65`: SCREAMING_SNAKE, domain prefix, standard member for a generic condition): `PACKAGE_` prefix beside the door's own `PACKAGE_DELETE_PARTIAL` / `PACKAGE_DELETE_FAILED` / `PACKAGE_PUBLISH_FAILED` (`@objectstack/rest`, `:263-266`); `RESTRICTED` is the standard catalog's own word for a 409 refused over a dependent (`DELETE_RESTRICTED`, "Cannot delete due to dependencies", `errors.zod.ts:97`); the `_BY_CAUSE` tail has a precedent (`ORGANIZATION_SLUG_LOCKED_BY_ACTIVE_ENVIRONMENTS`, `:600`). Meaning does not collide: `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` says which object is withheld, `WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED` refuses the same verb on a read-only package (`:508-514`), `DEPENDENCY_MISSING` reads `manifest.dependencies` (`:733-746`), and the standard `DELETE_RESTRICTED` names a delete, not a disable. Right.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/30724-package-disable-dependent-rule-code.md`: `@objectstack/spec: patch`, body carries `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`; PR body carries the same two lines. **`patch` is the repo's rule, not a deviation**: AGENTS.md "Add a changeset" (lines 1026-1028) — "The level follows the kind alone: a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves, `none` takes `patch`; a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`" — and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`'s level axis (ruling A on #25105, `:899-912`, verdicts `none-clean` / `none-minor` in `judgeLevel`) refuses a `minor` under `none`. The dispatch's `minor` expectation predates ruling A; the seat-accepted "deviation" in the dev report is in fact conformance.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: an error code is wire vocabulary a consumer branches on, not a key, value or type a metadata author writes.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right: the ledger header (`:101-102`) names a registration a Clause-② widening, door or no door. The `Check Changeset` run on the head is `success`.
- `skip-changeset`: not applicable; `@objectstack/spec` publishes the row.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag "the triage note says the code is already served; it is not" — **answered, dev is right**: `packages.ts:1950-1981` on `main` runs permission, wall, query, read-only and `disablePackage`/404 checks and nothing else; no dependent scan, no 409, and the spelling has no hit on `origin/main`. Triage 6672694111's sentence is wrong and not a defect of this PR.
- Dev flag "`patch`, not `minor`" — answered in ②: conformance, not deviation.
- Dev flag "companion tables checked, none owes a row" — answered in ①: confirmed against each table on `main`.
- Dev flag "serial follower #30379 … error-catalog guard wants a heading if a 409 is published" — answered: true reading of `check-error-status-conformance.mjs:39-56`; carried to #30379 (see ④).
- `open_questions: []` — nothing to escalate. The Docs Drift Check comment (6674967557) is advisory and lists no page this PR must edit; the two release-owned pages are read-only by guardrail.
- Claim scope held: the diff touches no `packages/runtime/**`, no other ledger row, no `retired-error-codes.ts`, no skills/ADR/AGENTS.md.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts` — judged against the ruling it implements (6670643454, letter A on #30379, ADR-0141 Open item 4) and its first consumer (the disable branch of `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts`, where #30379 will stamp it).

- **The row comment is true against the door and the ruling.** Each sentence checks: the door is `PATCH /packages/:id/disable` in `domains/packages.ts` (`:1950`); the refusal condition is an enabled package's validation rule reading a field this package adds through `objectExtensions` (ruling item 1); "any severity" and "an app's `.custom` pair" (ruling items 1-2); `409` (item 3); the message naming package · object · rule, one or several (item 3); formulas not refused, answering `null` (item 1, PR #30362's pin); the remedy (card Ask, bullet 2); "registered AHEAD of its producer" (true on `main`, ① provenance). The `*_DISABLED` disambiguation reuses the ledger's own `ACTION_DISABLED` reasoning (`:381-387`: those codes say WHICH thing is off); the `DEPENDENCY_MISSING` disambiguation is accurate to that row (`:733-746`).
- **Tried to break it.** (a) A client that already branches on `DELETE_RESTRICTED` for 409s at `/packages`: the door answers no standard 409 today, so nothing is re-routed. (b) Could the door answer `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` or `WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED` instead? The first is the generic member the ruling refused in favour of a new code; the second names a different condition (read-only package) with a different remedy, and would send the operator to the wrong fix. (c) Could the condition be reported per rule under several codes (warning vs error severity)? The ruling fixes one refusal over every severity, so one code with the triples in the message is the right arity. (d) Does the row promise a `details` shape no door can keep? It does not: it promises a message naming the triples, which is exactly the ruling's wording. The design holds.
- **Must-fix: none.**
- **Should-fix: none** on the `hits` file.
- **Carry to #30379 (not findings on this PR):** (1) the stamp belongs in `domains/packages.ts` under `@objectstack/runtime`, ahead of `registry.disablePackage` (`:1973`) and after the read-only check, so no state moves before the refusal; `check:error-code-provenance` is then satisfied by this row alone. (2) If #30379 fixes an `error.details` shape for the triples, state it on this row's comment and in a `contracts/` schema the way `ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` does (`:344-346`); the ruling leaves it open. (3) `content/docs/deployment/marketplace-handbook.mdx:230,304` document the disable door's refusals (`422 WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED`) and will need the 409 row; if a page publishes the status, `error-catalog.mdx` then owes a heading for the code (`check-error-status-conformance`). (4) The ADR-0141 Open item 4 line is #30379's, per ruling item 4.

Check-runs on the head at review time: 42 runs — 13 `success` (incl. Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Spec property liveness, Dogfood Regression Gate), 7 `skipped`, 22 `in_progress` (Build Core, Build Docs, Test Core 1-8, Type Check ×4, Lint ×6, Live E2E UI), 0 `failure`. The in-progress families are not adopted by this record; their conclusions remain the gate verdicts and the queue guard holds the PR until they land. A red among them is a delta head for this seat.
